# Crypto — Web Crypto API Playground & Agentic Tool Server

> A browser-based cryptographic playground exposing 9 Web Crypto API algorithms as a hands-on form, an OpenAI-compatible AI agent chat with function calling, and W3C WebMCP tools. Everything runs client-side.

## Overview

The app lets a user (or an AI agent) select an algorithm, optionally pick a hash method or key length, generate keys, encrypt/decrypt or sign/verify, and inspect hex output. The same operations are exposed to AI agents in two ways:

1. **W3C WebMCP** — the page registers tools through `navigator.modelContext.provideContext({ tools })` in browsers that ship the API (feature-detected; clean no-op elsewhere).
2. **In-app AI chat** — a floating chat panel (Vuetify `v-bottom-sheet`/`v-dialog`) talks to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (LM Studio at `http://localhost:1234/v1` by default, Ollama, OpenAI, OpenRouter, or a custom URL) using OpenAI `tools`/`tool_calls`; results are rendered as cards inside the chat.

## Supported Algorithms

| Algorithm | Methods | Key lengths (bits) | Key generation | Inverted keys |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| DIGEST | SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512 | — | no | no |
| AES-CBC | — | 128, 192, 256 | yes | no |
| AES-CTR | — | 128, 192, 256 | yes | no |
| AES-GCM | — | 128, 192, 256 | yes | no |
| RSA-OAEP | SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512 | 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 | yes | yes |
| RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 | SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512 | 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 | yes | yes |
| RSA-PSS | SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512 | 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 | yes | yes |
| ECDSA | SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512 | 256, 384, 521 | yes | yes |
| HMAC | SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512 | 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 | yes | no |

"Inverted" means the private key sits on the sender side (signing) and the public key on the recipient side (verification).

## Data Formats

- All keys and ciphertexts are lowercase hex strings.
- AES-CBC/CTR/GCM ciphertext embeds the 128-bit IV as a prefix: `hex(iv) || hex(ciphertext)`.
- Asymmetric keys are imported from raw hex (SPKI for public, PKCS#8 for private).

## Agent Tools (WebMCP and OpenAI function calling)

The tool registry at `src/agent/toolRegistry.ts` defines five tools:

### list_algorithms

Returns every supported algorithm with its methods, key lengths, generation and inversion flags. Takes no arguments.

### compute_digest

Hashes text into a hex digest. Parameters: `text` (string, required), `method` (one of SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512; defaults to SHA-256).

### generate_keys

Generates a symmetric key or a public/private key pair. Parameters: `algorithm` (required), `method` (optional), `length` (optional; defaults to the first configured length). Returns `public` and `private` hex strings.

### encrypt_or_sign

Encrypts text (AES-*, RSA-OAEP) or produces a signature/MAC (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, RSA-PSS, ECDSA, HMAC). Parameters: `algorithm` (required), `text` (required), `key` (hex key; may be omitted when `autoGenerateKey` is true), `method`, `length`, `autoGenerateKey` (boolean). Returns the hex output (and generated keys when applicable).

### decrypt_or_verify

Decrypts ciphertext (AES-*, RSA-OAEP) or verifies a signature/MAC. Parameters: `algorithm` (required), `ciphertextOrSignature` (required), `key` (required hex), `originalText` (required for signatures), `method`, `length`. Returns the plaintext, or `verifyStatus` for signatures.

All handlers are pure client-side Web Crypto calls: read-only, idempotent, no network access, no persistence.

## AI Chat Configuration

The floating chat panel stores its settings in `localStorage`:

- **Base URL** — defaults to `http://localhost:1234/v1` (LM Studio). Presets for Ollama (`http://localhost:11434/v1`), OpenAI (`https://api.openai.com/v1`), OpenRouter (`https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`) and custom.
- **API key** — optional for LM Studio; stored only in the browser.
- **Model** — fetched from `GET {baseUrl}/models` and selectable via a combobox.

Tool calling uses the OpenAI `tools` parameter; when a model lacks native `tool_calls`, a JSON block fallback (`{"tool": "...", "arguments": {...}}`) is parsed from the message text. When the app is served over HTTPS and points at a local HTTP endpoint, enable CORS in LM Studio (`lms server start --cors`).
